property_summary: When initialize() is called without setting nft, the reference's availableForFlashLoan reverts because nft remains address(0) and not initialized, whereas the buggy contract also reverts; but since the difference is that initialized is set to true in both after initialize(), we need a scenario where after initialize() the reference sets nft so availableForFlashLoan succeeds and initialized remains true, while the buggy contract does not set nft so availableForFlashLoan reverts and initialized remains true — the divergence is not on initialized. The actual difference is that in the buggy contract, nft is never set, so calling availableForFlashLoan with any token that is not owned by the pool will return false because ERC721.ownerOf will revert (since nft is zero address) and catch returns false, while in the reference nft is set so ownerOf succeeds and returns the pool address if the token is deposited. So the concrete scenario: initialize the pool with nft = address(1), deposit token id 0 from address(1) into the pool, then availableForFlashLoan(address(1), 0) returns true in reference but false in bug (since bug's nft is zero address, ownerOf reverts).
change_summary: Delete the statement that sets nft
